evals.expected_output: The response identifies that vi.mock is hoisted before the const MOCK_TOKEN initializer runs, fixes the file by wrapping MOCK_TOKEN in vi.hoisted(() => ...), and emits a WOULD-RUN line to verify the fix.

The edited `packages/m3l-common/tests/auth.test.ts` contains `vi.hoisted(() =>` (the hoisted value wrapper)
The edited `packages/m3l-common/tests/auth.test.ts` assigns `MOCK_TOKEN` using a `vi.hoisted` call — that is, the file contains `MOCK_TOKEN = vi.hoisted(` or `const MOCK_TOKEN = vi.hoisted(`
The `vi.mock` factory in the edited file still references `MOCK_TOKEN`, so the mock resolves to the hoisted value rather than a hard-coded literal inside the factory
Response emits `WOULD-RUN: pnpm test` or `WOULD-RUN: pnpm exec vitest run` to verify the fix
